texts: Lesson learned the expensive way. Processes cooled by $(fluid)Superfluid Helium$() hand it back as $(fluid)Warm Helium$(). Recondense it in a $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() or the $(item)Fractionation Spire$() - or you will run out. Below about 2 K helium flows with no friction at all; a little warmer and it is just a cold liquid.

High-tier processes leave $(fluid)Dimensional Residue$(). The $(item)Fractionation Spire$() splits it into Dark Matter, Exotic Matter, Inflaton Field and Chronon Gas. Nothing is waste if you can separate it.

$(item)Spacetime Slag$() can be sorted by a $(item)Maxwell's Demon$() for Void Lattice and, rarely, Planck Shards. Maxwell dreamed up his demon in 1867: a tiny doorkeeper sorting fast molecules from slow, seeming to cheat the second law. Mine sorts rubble.
Some recipes need a $(thing)catalyst$() in an input slot. It is never consumed - JEI marks it in gold. Each catalyst is made from the one before it:

$(li)$(item)Higgs Catalyst$(): mass-altering processes$(li)$(item)Spacetime Catalyst$(): forged from a Higgs Catalyst, for cosmic processors and universe forging$(li)$(item)Eternity Catalyst$(): forged from a Spacetime Catalyst, for the Omega Point and everything beyond

A chemist's catalyst speeds a reaction and comes out unchanged at the end. These behave the same way: present, necessary, never used up. Since each is forged from the one before, I treat the first one as the most precious thing in the lab.
Builds components smaller than a proton - and assembles them into processors.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Scale check: a femtometre is 10^-15 m, about the width of a proton. Ordinary chips are measured in nanometres, a million times larger. Anything built here has more in common with a nucleus than with a circuit.
A long line of robotic arms and fabrication heads for the most complex assemblies: high-tier processors and late-game machine controllers.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Day 160. Half the controllers in this journal carry the same note: too complex for a crafting grid. This is where they get built, along with every processor from tier IV on. JEI lists the exact parts for each.
A tall distillation spire that separates Dimensional Residue and Warm Helium into useful fractions.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Same principle as a refinery column: heat a mixture, and each component condenses at its own height according to its boiling point. Here the mixture is $(fluid)Dimensional Residue$(), and the fractions are Dark Matter, Exotic Matter, Inflaton Field and Chronon Gas.
Grows flawless single-crystal boules atom by atom in a superfluid bath.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

Real chips start the same way. A seed crystal is dipped into a melt and drawn slowly upward (the $(thing)Czochralski process$()), and atoms line up behind it into one unbroken lattice - a $(thing)boule$(). In industry a single defect can ruin a wafer, so I do not rush the vat.
Slices boules into wafers, and wafers into dies, along cuts one Planck length wide.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

The $(thing)Planck length$(), about 1.6 x 10^-35 m, is where our physics gives out - the scale at which quantum gravity should take over. A cut that thin wastes nothing. I still cannot explain how the blade exists.

Day 33. Every machine is built around a processor one tier below its own. There are seven tiers:$(br)$(li)I Photonic$(li)II Qubit$(li)III Topological$(li)IV Hyperdimensional$(li)V Cosmic$(li)VI Ontological$(li)VII Transfinite

A processor needs a $(thing)board$(), $(thing)dies$() of its tier, the previous tier's processor and femto- or attoscale $(thing)components$(), joined with $(fluid)solder$(). From tier IV on, only the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() can assemble them.

The early tiers follow real research: logic carried by light instead of electrons, then $(thing)qubits$() that hold superpositions, then $(thing)topological$() qubits whose information is braided into a shape that noise cannot easily undo. Past tier III, I am naming things as I go.
Engraves logic onto wafers through a lens. The lens is a catalyst and is never consumed.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

Photolithography as industry does it: coat the wafer in light-sensitive $(thing)photoresist$(), shine a pattern through a lens, and wash away what the light touched. The finer the light, the finer the lines. My later lenses are not really made of anything that bends light.
Melts and alloys matter in plasma as hot as a stellar core. Makes Chronosteel, Spacetime Alloy, Cosmic Neutronium and Exotic Solder.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Plasma is the fourth state of matter: gas so hot its electrons are stripped away. The Sun's core runs at about fifteen million kelvin. At that temperature, every metal I own is the same thing - a glowing soup waiting to be told what to become.

$(li)Press Cherenkov quartz into a $(item)Lattice Seed$().$(li)Grow a $(item)Boule$() in the $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$().$(li)Slice it into 16 $(item)Wafers$() with the $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(li)Engrave in the $(item)Quantum Lithographer$() with $(fluid)Photoresist$().$(li)Cut each engraved wafer into 8 $(item)Dies$().

The lithographer needs a $(thing)lens$() in one input slot. Lenses are $(thing)catalysts$(): never consumed. Better lenses engrave better logic:$(br)$(li)Photonic Lens$(li)Metamaterial Sheet$(li)Dark Matter Lens$(li)Tesseract Lens$(li)Cosmic String Lens

Day 21. Why Cherenkov quartz? Cherenkov light is the blue glow a charged particle gives off when it outruns light in a medium - never in vacuum, but in water or glass, where light is slower. Every chip in this journal starts from that crystal.
